title: Broker Non-Payment Bond-Claim Collective for Small Carriers
one_liner: A service that files carriers' unpaid-load claims against the broker's surety bond and FMCSA record, pools every claimant against the same broker, and publishes a real days-to-pay broker score built from actual payment outcomes.
customer: Small carriers and owner-operators (1 to 10 trucks), including hot-shot and box-truck carriers who don't factor every load. A second revenue stream comes from carriers who pay to check brokers before hauling.
problem: Small unpaid loads are too small for a lawyer and too big to shrug off. One carrier reported a $600 CAD load completed in November 2025 still unpaid in June 2026, after 50+ emails and calls that got only automated replies from a 'Legal Dispute Department'. Their workaround was to 'sign up with factoring companies' who 'either approve or deny'. Meanwhile freight rates have stayed squeezed since 2022, so broker failures and slow payers keep coming.
solution: The carrier uploads the rate confirmation, proof of delivery and invoice. The service verifies the broker's authority and bond or trust-fund status from public FMCSA data, sends a formal demand, and files the claim with the broker's surety (federal rules require property brokers to carry financial security, at $75,000, which is paid out pro rata when many claimants exist). It files an FMCSA complaint and logs every step. The key mechanic is pooling: claims against the same broker are grouped so its claimants are first in line and can cite a pattern. All outcomes feed a broker pay-speed database ('median days to pay', 'claims filed', 'claims paid') that carriers check before booking a load. A trucking attorney reviews templates to stay clear of unauthorized-practice issues.
why_now: The freight recession is still going: the owner-operator thread 'Rates are crashing and fuel to the moon!' began in March 2022 and was on page 1,134 as of Sept 26, 2026. Squeezed brokers pay slowly or fail, and forums are full of fraud and non-payer alerts. Document-heavy claim filing can now be automated cheaply. Factoring companies increasingly reject unknown or slow brokers, which pushes more risk back to unfactored small carriers.
revenue_model: 20 to 25% contingency on recovered amounts. A $15 per month subscription for broker pay-speed lookups and alerts. Later, sell the broker payment-behavior data to factoring companies and load boards.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is not the collection letter but the payment-behavior data no credit bureau has, and it is created only by filing claims in bulk. The owner of one 'fraud alert' thread described 50+ emails and only automated replies over 7 months for a $600 CAD load, with a second victim in the same thread and factoring as the only workaround (https://www.thetruckersreport.com/truckingindustryforum/posts/13536421/). The margin squeeze is ongoing: the rates-and-fuel thread reached page 1,134 in Sept 2026 (https://www.thetruckersreport.com/truckingindustryforum/posts/13542683/). A new-authority owner-operator says he cannot get financing and rents a box truck by the day, missing about $4,000 a day in loads, which shows how thin small carriers' cash is (https://www.thetruckersreport.com/truckingindustryforum/posts/13465676/). The bond rule detail is from general knowledge of FMCSA broker financial-security requirements and needs legal confirmation.
first_30_days: Week 1: recruit a trucking attorney to review one claim template. Post in the TruckersReport Freight Broker forum offering free claim filing to carriers in the fraud-alert threads. Weeks 2 to 3: file 15 to 20 claims by hand, group them by broker, and record response times. Week 4: publish the first 'days-to-pay' leaderboard of 25 brokers, and start charging 20% contingency. Target: 30 claims filed and 5 paid, with the leaderboard as the top-of-funnel.

title: Air-Permit Unlock for Idle Data Center Diesel
one_liner: Turn the ~55 GW of idle data center backup generators into dispatchable capacity by solving the air-permit problem instead of the hardware problem.
customer: Colo and hyperscale operators in PJM (Northern Virginia, Ohio, Illinois) with 20-500 MW of backup gensets. Secondary buyers are utilities and capacity buyers who need fast MW.
problem: Data centers hold about 55 GW of backup diesel (Virginia alone has about 27 GW permitted), and it runs 10-30 minutes a month. PJM cleared 6.8 GW short and wants large loads to bring their own capacity or be curtailed. Air permits cap non-emergency run hours, so nobody can legally count these engines as capacity.
solution: Fixed-price 'permit-to-dispatch' packages. They cover a state-specific permit modification strategy (run-hour caps, synthetic-minor limits), engineering and financing for emissions retrofits on the subset of engines that need them, and paralleling/telemetry upgrades. Enrollment in PJM's on-site backup (IRAS-style) and demand-response programs comes with third-party measurement and verification. Runtime is capped at a few dozen to ~100 hours a year, dispatched only in system emergencies, with community disclosure built in.
why_now: PJM's July auction shortfall, the proposed backstop auction (15-year terms, $555/MW-day cap) and the curtailment-or-bring-capacity rule make backup generation valuable for the first time. Turbines are sold out until 2029-30, so this fleet is the only large block of capacity that exists today.
revenue_model: $40-150k fixed fee per site for permit and engineering work, plus 10-20% of the first five years of capacity revenue. At the $325/MW-day cap a 20 MW fleet is worth very roughly $1.5-2M a year after derating, so the fee is easy to justify. Retrofit financing adds a spread.
non_obvious_insight: The cheapest big block of new PJM capacity is not new. It is already built and sitting behind a fence, and the barrier is air-permit lawyering that VC-backed hardware companies ignore. A repeatable per-state permit playbook is the moat. Emergency-only runtime is why it works: at under 1% of hours, the capacity value dwarfs the emissions.
first_30_days: Pull public Title V and minor-source permit files for ~30 colo sites in VA, OH and IL. Build a 'permit headroom map' showing run-hour caps and engine tiers. Retain one air-permitting consultant. Offer 25 facility and sustainability leads a $15k fixed-fee dispatch-readiness audit of a 20+ MW fleet and aim to close two paid pilots.

title: Placement Proof for Workforce Pell Providers
one_liner: A verified job-placement and completion ledger that makes short-term training programs (CDL, CNA, welding, HVAC, medical assistant, cosmetology) audit-ready for the governor and Secretary approvals that Workforce Pell requires.
customer: Small proprietary career schools, community college workforce and continuing-education units, and employer-training nonprofits running 8-15 week programs. The program owner or director pays. State workforce boards are a second buyer because they were given no new resources to verify placement.
problem: The Workforce Pell final rule (published May 19, 2026; effective July 20, 2026, with early implementation from July 1) covers programs of 150-599 clock hours and 8-15 weeks. A program must show 70% completion and 70% job placement, measured over the 12 months before it applies and annually after that. The governor must first certify the program as high-skill, high-wage or in-demand, then the Secretary approves. Providers must submit completer lists and the information needed to verify placement. Commenters flagged burden for small providers and noted states got no new resources to run the framework. Separately, the earnings-premium rule (effective July 1, 2027) strips Direct Loan access from programs that fail in two of three consecutive years. The Department estimated 93% of cosmetology programs would fail under the proposal.
solution: At completion the system automatically sends completers and employers text and email verification requests at 30, 90 and 180 days. It collects pay stubs, employer confirmations and consent for state wage-record matching, and reconciles them to the rule's placement definition. It produces the governor's application packet (completer list, placement evidence, tuition versus earnings benchmarks) and the annual recertification. It also scores each existing program's exposure to the earnings-premium test using public program-level earnings data so owners can decide what to keep, fix or convert into a short-term program.
why_now: The 12-month look-back means a provider that is not tracking verified placement now cannot apply in 2027. The earnings-premium test takes effect July 1, 2027 and is already being scored on 2021 completers' 2025 earnings. States are building governor-approval processes this fall, and Workforce Pell went live July 2026.
revenue_model: $4-12k per year per program subscription, or $150-300 per completer verified. $3-5k fixed fee for the governor application packet. Earnings-premium exposure report for $1.5-3k. Later, licensing to state workforce boards for verification.
non_obvious_insight: The binding constraint is not program design but evidence: 70% verified placement with a 12-month clock that starts before the application. Short-course providers such as CDL, CNA and barbering schools typically track completion, not verified employment, so most will discover the gap after the clock has started. The final rule requires providers to give the Governor 'necessary information to verify the job placement rate', and it aggregates small programs' completers up to four award years to reach a 30-student minimum, which favors providers with clean historical records. The Title IV survival angle (93% of cosmetology programs were projected to fail the earnings test under the proposal) gives the same customer a second, more urgent reason to buy. Sources: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/19/2026-10013/accountability-in-higher-education-and-access-through-demand-driven-workforce-pell-pell-grant and https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/01/2026-13286/accountability-in-higher-education-and-access-through-demand--driven-workforce-pell-student-tuition
first_30_days: Pick two states whose governors have opened a Workforce Pell approval process. Recruit five schools in different fields, including one at-risk cosmetology school, with a $1.5k pilot price. Backfill the last 12 months of completers by text and employer email to produce a baseline verified placement rate. Deliver a sample governor packet and an earnings-premium exposure score for each. Use the results to pitch the state workforce board on verification capacity.

title: Real Gross Margin Diligence for AI Startups
one_liner: Quality-of-earnings for agent companies: restate COGS at unsubsidized token prices, retry waste and expiring credits so investors see true unit economics.
customer: Growth-equity, PE and VC diligence teams and corporate M&A groups acquiring AI-native companies ($20M-$500M deals), and startups preparing a raise.
problem: Reported AI gross margins are flattered by free cloud and model credits, introductory rates and uncosted retries. Practitioners say diligence restates credits at renewal prices, and AI-native margins run around 50-60% versus 75-85% for classic SaaS. Agentic tasks use 5-30x more tokens, so cohort economics move fast. M&A is heating up (Okta bought Permiso for about $200M in July 2026, and Palo Alto bought Portkey and Koi). Traditional QoE firms lack telemetry fluency.
solution: Read-only connectors to billing exports, gateways, cloud invoices and product analytics. Produce cohort-level unsubsidized COGS per seat or outcome, sensitivity to price cuts and model swaps, tokens per customer growth, cost of failed runs and retries, and scaling curves. Five-day turnaround report, plus quarterly monitoring for fund portfolios.
why_now: An AI M&A wave and investors pricing trajectory over current margin. Credit-inflated margins matter more as promotional pricing expires, and 73% of enterprises overran AI budgets.
revenue_model: $15-$40k per diligence engagement and $3-$8k/month portfolio monitoring subscriptions for funds.
non_obvious_insight: The margin story is hidden in gateway and billing logs, not the general ledger. Buyers pay a premium to avoid overpaying for subsidized revenue, and every engagement builds a private benchmark of credit-adjusted margins.
first_30_days: Write the data-request list and report template. Pitch 20 growth-stage funds and deal associates, deliver 2 discounted diligence reports, and publish an anonymized credit-adjusted gross margin benchmark to generate inbound.

title: Co-op Ledger Signals: Farm Distress Early Warning
one_liner: Benchmark co-ops on their own receivables, then sell the anonymized, county-level 'who is paying whom first' data to lenders, insurers and equipment financiers as a leading indicator of farm distress.
customer: First payers: co-op managers and CFOs, who buy the benchmark dashboard. Data buyers: Farmer Mac, Farm Credit institutions, regional ag banks, equipment captive finance arms, input manufacturers, ag reinsurers and funds trading farm-exposed equities.
problem: Ag bank delinquency stats and Fed surveys lag reality by two to three quarters. Meanwhile every co-op ERP quietly holds the earliest signal: accounts-receivable aging by customer, the timing of input payments, and who is asking for deferred-payment or extended-terms deals. Farmers in trouble pay in a predictable order (operating lender, landlord, seed, then the co-op), so slow co-op payments show up long before defaults. Each co-op sees only its own trade area and cannot tell whether its collection problems are local or systemic.
solution: Ship a free-to-cheap benchmark: connect the co-op's grain and ag-retail accounting system (Agvance, Agris and similar) and get peer comparisons on A/R over 90 days, prepay behavior, and credit-line usage. In return, contribute anonymized data to a pooled index with strict privacy rules (a minimum of 5 co-ops per cell, county-by-month, no farmer-level data). Sell the county-level Farm Payment Stress Index to lenders and funds, with a second SKU for weekly harvest-pace and grain-quality metrics (moisture, test weight, damage) from scale tickets. Co-ops receive a revenue share.
why_now: Chapter 12 filings are up sharply, the Chicago Fed reports rising loan rollovers and falling cash rents, and USDA projects record farm debt. Federal data proved brittle during the fall 2025 shutdown, and lenders and funds want independent ground truth without waiting for quarterly surveys.
revenue_model: Co-op benchmark subscription ($300 to $800 a month). Index licenses to lenders and reinsurers ($25k to $150k a year). Fund data feeds ($5k to $15k a month). Co-ops receive 40% to 50% of data revenue.
non_obvious_insight: The co-op's boring back-office ledger is the best real-time farm-distress sensor in America. Co-op managers think the data is too mundane to sell. The way to get it is to give them the peer benchmark they have always wanted and only then aggregate.
first_30_days: Recruit 5 to 8 co-ops through state co-op councils and CFO peer groups with a free 'A/R health check'. Build an ETL for the two or three most common co-op ERPs. Produce the first county-level index by Q4 2026. Pitch two ag lenders and one reinsurer for paid pilots.

title: Zero-Return Tax Desks Inside POS Agent Shops
one_liner: Turn trusted POS agent shops into walk-in compliance desks that get informal traders their TIN and filed small-company returns before the penalties bite.
customer: Informal and micro-traders and small registered businesses (turnover under about N100m) who need to file to claim the 0% small-company rate; POS agents who earn a revenue share; principals (banks and MFBs) who want stickier merchants.
problem: Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 the 0% small-company exemption (turnover about N100m or less and fixed assets under about N250m) is not automatic. You still need a TIN, records and an annual return even when tax due is zero. Filing penalties are now N100k in month one plus N50k per month after. E-invoicing reaches medium taxpayers from July 2026 and small ones from July 2027. Most shop owners are terrified of 'tax people', do not own a smartphone workflow, and cannot afford an accountant at N50-150k. Agents already see their shop's real turnover every day but never use it.
solution: A shop-counter service where the agent collects CAC, NIN and basic details on a tablet, and the platform pre-fills the TIN check and zero or small-company return using the shop's actual bank and POS statement history, with AI extraction from the pictures. A partner chartered accountant or tax practitioner reviews and signs. Recurring layer: monthly bookkeeping and a reminder feed. Later, e-invoice readiness (NRS Merchant Buyer Solution onboarding) for those crossing the next thresholds.
why_now: NTA 2025 and the Tax Administration Act took effect on 1 January 2026, with steep new late-filing penalties. The first e-invoicing go-live dates (July 2026 for medium taxpayers, July 2027 for emerging ones) are here. CBN's April 2026 single-principal rule has made agents look for non-banking revenue that keeps customers walking in. LLM extraction from photos and PDF statements is finally cheap and accurate.
revenue_model: About N7,500-15,000 per annual return, with 30-40% going to the agent. A N2,000-3,000 per month bookkeeping and reminder subscription. Referral fees from principals and accountants. Enterprise deals to give principals a white-label tax-desk feature for their agent networks.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is trust and fear, not software, and the person who has it is the agent who has known the trader for five years. Agents also hold the one thing no tax app has: 12-24 months of a shop's real transaction history. Small-company status is a 'file to be free' product, not a 'pay tax' product, so the pitch to a trader is saving a N100k fine, not helping the government.
first_30_days: Partner with one ICAN/ANAN/CITN-registered accountant who reviews and signs. Recruit 30 agents in one Lagos market cluster (for example Ikeja or Yaba) from agent WhatsApp groups. Run a 'file before the fines' campaign at N5,000 introductory price. Aim for 300 filings in 30 days, hand-checked, and document the objection patterns and the paperwork that trips people up.

title: Beaver Warranty for County Culverts and Roads
one_liner: A 5-year no-clog guarantee that keeps beavers out of culverts using flow devices and sensors, and later sells the wetlands they build to water and wildfire agencies.
customer: County and municipal public works departments, state DOTs and railroads, and later water utilities and wildfire agencies.
problem: Beavers plug culverts, flooding roads and forcing repeated trapping, dam breaching and clearing, which costs taxpayers every year and never ends because new beavers arrive. Managers have no reliable, maintenance-free alternative and little data on true costs.
solution: A fixed-price warranty that installs proven flow devices (culvert fences and pond levelers), adds low-cost water-level sensors and cameras, and covers every follow-up visit. Evidence in hand: Virginia's DOT spent more than $300,000 a year on prevention, repairs and removal before devices, versus under $45,000 for installation and $277 a year to maintain; and Billerica, MA found trapping and breaching cost $409 per site per year versus $229 for devices. Well-designed culvert fences reportedly succeed 95% of the time. Once the culvert is solved, we offer beaver dam analogs and habitat as water storage and fire refuge.
why_now: California's Beaver Restoration Program (2023) had received 26 proposals by April 2026, and CDFW grants have funded over 100 beaver dam analogs. Wildfire and drought budgets are looking for nature-based solutions. Cheap IoT level sensors make a guarantee affordable to price and monitor.
revenue_model: Installs of roughly $8-45k per site or bundle, an annual monitoring and warranty fee of $300-1,000, and later performance contracts with water and fire agencies for stored water or refuge acres.
non_obvious_insight: The county does not pay to deal with beavers, it pays for recurring emergency labor, so sell an insurance-style warranty backed by data, not a wildlife product. After the culvert is fixed, the beaver becomes a free crew building water storage that a different agency will pay for, so the same animal is a liability line item for one customer and an asset for another.
first_30_days: File public-records requests in five counties for trapping and culvert-clearing spend. Offer to fix the three worst culverts at cost in exchange for cost data and a case study, then sell sub-$50k warranties that fit under small-purchase thresholds.

title: GLP-1 Off-Ramp Program for Cash-Pay Prescribers
one_liner: A structured 12-week landing program for people stopping GLP-1 drugs, sold to the prescribers who lose revenue the day a patient quits.
customer: Independent obesity-medicine clinics, med spas and cash-pay telehealth prescribers (pay per enrollee); secondary: patients paying $149-249 for the program.
problem: Every fitness and nutrition company is building for people ON the drug. But real-world data suggest up to roughly 65 percent quit within a year, and a 2026 meta-regression finds about 60 percent of lost weight returns within a year of stopping (individual studies vary). The discontinuation moment is unowned: prescribers lose the patient, gyms never see them, and regain triggers shame and churn.
solution: A program keyed to the last-dose date: taper coordination with the prescriber, protein and resistance-training progression, weekly connected-scale weigh-ins, human coach check-ins on hunger and food noise, and pre-agreed re-start triggers (for example +3 percent regain) that route the patient back to the prescriber. Delivered by app plus partner gyms.
why_now: Oral GLP-1s at $149-299 cash (Wegovy pill launched Dec 2025/Jan 2026, orforglipron in April 2026) make starting cheap and stopping easy; about 1 in 8 US adults report currently taking one; cash-pay churn is the biggest leak in prescriber P&Ls.
revenue_model: $150-300 per enrollee paid by the prescriber as a retention and win-back tool (or $199 patient-paid), plus a revenue share on patients who restart therapy.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer is the prescriber, not the patient: the off-ramp is a retention product for the clinic's P&L, and a regain alert doubles as a win-back lead. Evidence on who regains is mixed, so a regain-risk model built from your own cohort becomes the proprietary asset.
first_30_days: Sign 3-5 independent clinics or med spas, enroll 30 patients ending therapy using an off-the-shelf connected scale, messaging tool and a lifting template, and track 90-day weight, lean-mass proxy and restart rate versus each clinic's history to use as the sales proof.

title: EU Liable-Party-of-Record for AI Products
one_liner: The registered agent of the AI era: an insured EU entity that stands as authorised representative under the new Product Liability Directive and keeps clients' evidence court-ready.
customer: Non-EU makers (10-200 staff) of AI-enabled consumer hardware and apps, such as robot vacuums, wearables, AI toys, smart-home and e-mobility firmware, selling into the EU via Amazon, Shopify or retailers.
problem: From 9 Dec 2026 software and AI count as 'products' under Directive 2024/2853. Courts can order disclosure of evidence, a defendant who stonewalls faces a presumption of defect, and liability cascades to importers, authorised representatives and fulfilment providers when no EU manufacturer exists. Small non-EU firms have no solvent EU counterparty, no organised technical file, and no cover. Marketplaces and logistics partners will start demanding all three.
solution: A fixed-fee service with four parts. (1) An EU entity acting as authorised representative and liable operator of record. (2) A 'disclosure-ready dossier': model and version registry, safety case, incident and OTA-update logs, and retention rules, collected through simple exports so a court order can be met in days. (3) EU-language complaint and defect intake plus recall coordination. (4) A bundled PLD policy through a fronting carrier or MGA, priced lower because the dossier removes unknowns.
why_now: The transposition deadline is 9 Dec 2026, about ten weeks away, and products placed on the market after it fall under the new regime. Only a minority of member states have finished transposing, so uncertainty peaks now. The December 2024 GPSR rule created a wave of paid 'EU responsible person' services, which shows small sellers buy this kind of compliance. Carriers filing broad AI exclusions (AIG, Berkley, Great American, ISO CG 40 47/48) push AI firms toward affirmative cover.
revenue_model: $1.5k-6k per month per client by risk tier, a $5-15k onboarding fee for the dossier, 10-15% commission on the bundled policy, and incident-response retainers. 40 clients at about $3k per month is roughly $1.4M ARR.
non_obvious_insight: The PLD creates an evidence-access war (disclosure orders plus presumptions of defect), and small firms lose it by default because they cannot produce coherent records. What clients buy is not legal advice but a solvent, present EU party who can hand a court a clean file. Demand will arrive through the distribution chain first, because retailers and marketplaces will impose it by contract before any regulator enforces it.
first_30_days: Partner with an EU product-liability law firm (NL, IE or DE) for the entity and an opinion letter. Publish a 10-page 'PLD readiness for AI hardware' guide. Pitch it to GPSR-rep leads, hardware accelerator alumni and Amazon/Shopify hardware sellers. Sign 5 founding clients at $1k per month. Get one European MGA or Lloyd's coverholder to quote the bundled policy.

title: Shared-Docket Lawsuits Against Scam Infrastructure
one_liner: Turn Google's and Microsoft's civil-seizure playbook into a membership where 20-50 mid-size banks and brands co-file one John Doe action against the kit or ring impersonating all of them.
customer: Regional banks, credit unions, toll and payment operators, and mid-market retail and logistics brands that are repeatedly impersonated. They are too small to fund a $1M lawsuit alone.
problem: Takedown notices are whack-a-mole. Criminal enforcement takes years, and the FBI is warning about $1.6B+ in law-enforcement impersonation alone. Phishing kits sell for about $50, and one E-ZPass smishing ring sent 330,000 texts a day and took about $1B over 3 years. Big Tech gets ex parte orders to seize domains and servers, but mid-size victims are left with abuse reports.
solution: An evidence-and-litigation-ops company paired with an independent law firm (fees billed separately, to respect fee-splitting rules). It continuously builds dossiers on the kits hitting its members and drafts one multi-plaintiff John Doe complaint (Lanham Act, CFAA, RICO where apt). It then obtains TRO and preliminary-injunction orders that compel registrars, registries, hosts, CDNs, and stablecoin issuers to act. Members pay a retainer plus a per-seizure fee and receive the takedown results.
why_now: Google's 2025 suit against the operators of the Lighthouse smishing kit and Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit seizures created templates and precedents. Kits are centralized, so one order can protect hundreds of brands. The US-UK agreement to coordinate scam-center takedowns (Sep 4 2026) signals political tailwind for civil action.
revenue_model: $2-5K per month per member. 30 members is roughly $1M ARR. Success fees per seized infrastructure cluster. Legal costs passed through.
non_obvious_insight: Litigation cost scales with the number of defendant networks, not the number of victims, so it works like a reverse class action: fixed cost, split N ways. Kit concentration means a single order hits infrastructure serving hundreds of brands. Everyone assumes only Microsoft and Google can afford this, and nobody sells it as a shared product.
first_30_days: Retain a boutique IP/cyber litigation firm. Recruit 5 founding members through a credit-union league or toll-operator association. Deliver each an evidence dossier on the kit currently hitting them. Pre-sell $2K/month founding memberships to fund the first filing within about 90 days.

title: Depot Finder for Robotaxi Fleets
one_liner: A power-first site database and brokerage matching robotaxi fleets to half-empty garages, office podiums and big-box lots with unused electric service.
customer: Robotaxi fleet operators and their depot partners (AV company real-estate teams and fleet contractors such as Moove, Avis and Lyft's Flexdrive) in launch cities, and owners of distressed garages and office podiums.
problem: AV fleets need charging and cleaning depots near service zones with megawatts of power and workable zoning, while utility interconnection takes 18-36 months. Meanwhile downtown garages and office podiums have oversized electrical service and falling parking revenue.
solution: A ranked site database using proximity to service zones, available service capacity (utility maps and permits), zoning and neighbor tolerance. We broker the lease, run pre-development diligence and later sell a 'depot-in-a-box' kit.
why_now: Waymo and others have announced 2026 expansion to many more metros using fleet partners, interconnection is the chokepoint, and office and parking distress is deep.
revenue_model: Broker fee of 4-6% of first-year rent, $5-10K per month site-package subscriptions from fleets, and landowner listing fees.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce resource is electric service already in place, and 'obsolete' vacant buildings hold plenty. The best robotaxi real estate may be a half-empty garage with a multi-megawatt service, not airport-adjacent industrial land.
first_30_days: Compile 300 candidate sites in two launching metros. Call the local depot leads at fleet operators and deliver a 'power-ready shortlist' for $5K. Sign one or two exclusive landowner listings.

title: Sub-Tier Surge Twin for the Industrial Base
one_liner: A digital twin of foundries, forges and motor makers that shows which supplier breaks first in a 180-day fight.
customer: Defense primes' supply-chain risk teams, private equity funds rolling up defense suppliers, DoD industrial-base offices, and sub-tier lenders.
problem: Leaders doubt they can sustain the 90-, 120- or 180-day fight and lack integrated supply-chain visibility. AIA-Bain identifies castings, forgings, sensors, semiconductors and solid rocket motors as bottlenecks. Private equity invests only $1-3B a year and is flying blind on capacity.
solution: Build a network model of sub-tier capacity from public and commercial data (facility permits, trade flows, workforce, energy use, certifications), calibrated by supplier surveys. Run agent-based surge scenarios to identify chokepoints and invest-or-acquire targets. Start with one commodity, castings and forgings.
why_now: The record defense funding wave is looking for bottlenecks to fund. Maven-scale AI targeting has raised concern about munition depth. Agentic simulation and cheap data enrichment make a 5-person twin feasible.
revenue_model: $60-250K per year per subscribing prime or fund, plus deal-sourcing fees on roll-up acquisitions.
non_obvious_insight: The people who will pay first are private equity funds hunting acquisition targets, not the Pentagon. The twin's early output is a target list for whoever wants to roll up the base.
first_30_days: Map 300 casting and forging plants from public data and publish a bottleneck brief. Present to 5 PE funds and 3 primes' supply-chain teams. Sign one paid pilot for a commodity view.

title: True Pop: De-duplicated Card Scarcity Data
one_liner: A data product that uses image matching to remove crack-and-resubmit double counts from graded-card population reports, showing lenders and dealers how many physical copies actually exist.
customer: Lenders and financiers that take graded cards as collateral, high-end dealers and auction houses, investment-minded collector groups, and insurers pricing slabs.
problem: Population reports count submissions, not unique cards. A card that is cracked and resubmitted is counted twice unless the owner mails back the slip, which most do not. Yet prices, loans and low-pop premiums key off those numbers. With a roughly 12x price gap between PSA 10 and PSA 9 at the top, the incentive to resubmit is enormous, so the most valuable cards are the most double-counted.
solution: For the top ~500 cards by value, ingest public cert-lookup images and sale photos and compute surface fingerprints (print defects, edge whitening, dings) to link cert numbers that are the same physical card. Publish a True Pop and a scarcity-adjusted price index, then add cert-duplicate alerts for buyers at purchase time.
why_now: A PSA 10 Pikachu Illustrator sold for $16.5M in Feb 2026, and cards are now used as loan collateral. Vision models make surface matching cheap. The pop report is treated as truth precisely as the money grows.
revenue_model: API and subscriptions of $300-2,000/month for lenders and dealers, $9 per-card reports for collectors, and data licensing to marketplaces.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone treats the pop report as the scarcity ground truth, so scarcity is systematically mispriced in one direction, and it is worst exactly where the dollars are. The wedge is a corrected number that lenders can underwrite against.
first_30_days: Hand-verify duplicates on 200 high-value cards using public cert pages. Publish a free weekly True Pop on X and Reddit for reach. Sell 3 pilot reports at $500 to dealers or lenders and interview 5 lenders. Get legal review of scraping and terms of use first, and use only public or user-submitted data.

title: Orphan-Element Audits for Copper Concentrate and Tailings
one_liner: A 90-day survey that measures the tellurium, selenium, bismuth, cobalt, germanium, rhenium, indium and scandium copper mines already ship for free, then brokers by-product credit rights with refiners.
customer: Mid-size copper miners (Arizona, Utah, Nevada, Chile, Peru, Zambia, Kazakhstan) who sell concentrate to smelters or run SX-EW, paying $40-120k per site survey. Refiners and specialty-metal buyers (Aurubis-type smelters, Umicore, 5N Plus-type processors) pay finder fees. Government programmes such as DoD DPA Title III and DLA support recovery projects.
problem: Smelter contracts pay for Cu, Au and Ag. Te, Se, Bi, Co, Ge, In, Sb and Re are either given away, or shown only as penalty elements (As, Sb, Bi, Hg, F). The plant lab measures the penalty elements and stops. The 48-element ICP-MS suite exists only on exploration drill core from ten years ago and never on the concentrate, tailings, SX raffinate or electrolyte bleed streams. The smelter quietly captures value in anode slimes and flue dust. The miner has no data to negotiate with. Meanwhile, benchmark treatment charges for 2026 reportedly collapsed to around zero, so smelters are squeezed and newly hunting for by-product margin and for clean feed. Chinese export controls on Te, Bi, In, Ga, Ge, Sb and others make Western buyers desperate.
solution: A productised survey: pull 30-60 retained samples from process streams (every mine keeps monthly composite retains), run multi-element ICP-MS plus automated mineralogy through partner labs, and deliver an 'orphan-element balance' showing tonnes per year and contained value per element. Then hand the mine a negotiation kit: by-product participation clauses for offtake contracts, dust and slime credit language, and penalty-threshold renegotiation. Route the data to refiners and toll processors who can recover the element. The compensation is a survey fee plus 10-20% of by-product margin for 5 years, or a finder fee at contract signing.
why_now: In 2025 China imposed export controls on tellurium, bismuth, indium, gallium, germanium and antimony, with rare earths restrictions following. US and EU strategic stockpile, offtake and grant programmes now pay for domestic by-product supply. Smelters are under profit pressure from near-zero treatment charges and are open to sharing upside with suppliers. Prices for Te and Bi jumped.
revenue_model: $40-120k per site survey, plus a 10-20% by-product royalty or finder fee on recovered element revenue, plus a refiner-side subscription for a pipeline of quantified feed.
non_obvious_insight: The barrier is not technology. Kennecott has produced tellurium for decades. It is that nobody measured, so nobody owns the value, and contracts were signed when no one cared. The person who knows how the process streams flow (where it goes to anode slimes, where to dust) can tell which stream concentrates each element.
first_30_days: Ask ten friendly mid-tier mines for retained composite samples, or buy access to public tailings and concentrate assays. Run 15 multi-element packs at $60-150 each (about $2k in total). Produce a one-page 'value at stake' per mine and email it to 30 operations and commercial managers. Sell 2-3 pilot surveys at $25k. Meanwhile call two refiners and one federal programme office with the resulting map to line up demand.

title: Storm-Chaser Livestreams as Claims Evidence
one_liner: License the timestamped, geotagged archives of storm-chaser channels as address-level date-of-loss evidence for hail, wind and flood claims.
customer: Public adjusters, policyholder attorneys and roofing-claim desks in hail states (Colorado, Texas, Nebraska, Minnesota) first. Parametric hail and wind MGAs and appraisal umpires second.
problem: Hail claims turn on whether hail of a given size hit an address on a given date. Radar estimates are error-prone at swath edges, and spotter reports are sparse. Hail drives 26-54% of Colorado premiums (secondary source). Colorado's HB25-1182 (in force since July 2026) and California's AB 75 give owners disclosure and appeal rights, but the evidence burden stays on them ('owners still have to prove their case'). Meanwhile storm chasers stream thousands of hours with GPS, timestamps and hailstones held next to coins, and that ground truth sits unmonetized on YouTube.
solution: Sign revenue-share licenses with chaser channels. Index their archives by time, location and hail size, using computer vision on reference objects, and pair each clip with radar. Sell a 'Date-of-Loss Dossier' per address: nearest verified clips, size estimate, uncertainty and chain of custody. Distribute a printed reference 'hail card' standard to chasers. Add a 'go verify' request queue where adjusters or parametric carriers post bounties on active storms and fans can top them up by tipping.
why_now: Storm-chase livestreaming is now a fan-funded media business with huge live audiences. New state laws create disputes that need evidence. Parametric MGAs need data that cuts basis risk. The 2025-26 hail seasons are still inside claim windows, and the spring 2027 season is six months away, so the archive-first version can sell now.
revenue_model: $39-149 per dossier from public adjusters and roofers, $2-5K a month API access for MGAs and claims shops, and 40-50% revenue share to creators.
non_obvious_insight: The densest hail sensor network in America is a fandom already paid for by fans. Insurers' problem is not data volume but admissible, attributable data, and chasers go exactly to the worst cell. Ground truth is a by-product of entertainment, so the sensor cost is already covered.
first_30_days: Approach 15 mid-size chaser channels (10K-300K subscribers) with a rev-share license for their 2024-26 archives. Index 200 hail events. Sell the first 50 dossiers to 5 Colorado and Texas public adjusters and roofing claim reps for open claims. Draft the reference-card standard for the spring 2027 season.

title: Mid-Term Premium True-Down for Shrinking Payrolls
one_liner: Monitor payroll against the estimate on a small business's workers' comp and liability policy, and file mid-term endorsements to cut inflated installments and misclassified codes.
customer: Small businesses with 10-200 employees and volatile payroll (trades, restaurants, staffing, light manufacturing) that already run payroll on Gusto, ADP, Rippling or QuickBooks, reached through CPAs and bookkeepers.
problem: Workers' comp and general liability premiums are priced on estimated payroll and revenue, and only reconciled at year-end audit. When headcount drops, the business keeps paying installments on inflated estimates, financing the insurer, often through premium finance at rising interest. Class-code misclassification (office staff coded as field staff) is also common. Brokers are paid a percentage of premium, so nobody is paid to lower it mid-term.
solution: Connect payroll data, compare actual payroll by class code with the policy estimate each month, generate the carrier endorsement request and support documents, and track the reduced installment schedule. Audit class codes and prepare audit-ready records. Offer optional pay-as-you-go workers' comp placement later.
why_now: Hiring freezes and layoffs are rising as the economy cools. Higher rates raise the cost of premium financing and make cash tighter. Payroll APIs are mature enough to automate the variance check.
revenue_model: 20% of the first-year realized premium reduction, or $49-99 per month SaaS. Partnerships with CPA firms and bookkeepers.
non_obvious_insight: The blocker is incentives, not technology. Brokers earn commission on premium, so no one in the chain is paid to file the endorsement. Downturns make the savings largest exactly when cash is scarcest.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 small businesses through two CPA or bookkeeper networks. Review each policy's declarations page against the last three months of payroll. File endorsements and misclassification challenges by hand, record the realized savings and set pricing at 20% of the first-year benefit.

title: Layoff Compliance Autopilot for Mid-Size HR
one_liner: Software plus expert review that generates every notice, filing and adverse-impact analysis a reduction-in-force needs, including a documented record of whether AI or restructuring drove each decision.
customer: HR and legal teams at 200-5,000-employee companies and the boutique employment law firms advising them pay $4-15k per event or $12-30k a year.
problem: RIF rules are fragmenting by state. New York's WARN form asks whether layoffs stem from AI or automation, New Jersey mandates severance, and OWBPA requires age disclosures for group terminations. Remote workforces span 20+ states. Mid-size firms rely on $500-an-hour outside counsel or spreadsheets while age-bias and AI-washing scrutiny (Mobley v. Workday) rises.
solution: Upload the roster and selection criteria. The tool maps each jurisdiction's rules, generates notices, separation agreements and OWBPA disclosures, runs adverse-impact statistics (age, race, sex, disability, leave) with remediation suggestions, and builds an AI-attribution record of task-level evidence for each decision. It includes a filing calendar and a lawyer-in-the-loop review queue.
why_now: Cuts are steady even though Challenger totals are down 41% year on year, AI is the leading cited reason, and NY added an AI checkbox in 2025. Age-discrimination class actions are live, and LLMs now make document generation cheap while lawyers still sign off.
revenue_model: Per-event fee ($4-15k), annual subscription, and revenue share with reselling law firms.
non_obvious_insight: The pain is not 'AI layoffs' but the compliance combinatorics of remote-first firms. The economic buyers (law firms and HR) either bill by the hour or bear the risk, and steady low-volume cuts mean repeated use.
first_30_days: Build a state-by-state rule matrix for the top 12 states plus federal rules. Sell $2,500 'RIF readiness packs' to 10 boutique employment firms. Run three live RIF events with friendly firms.

title: Dock Tax: Pricing Every Shipper Facility's Hidden Premium
one_liner: Use pooled broker quote and cover data to compute the exact per-load premium carriers add to any lane touching each bad dock, then sell shippers a ranked 'fix these five docks' report with dollar savings attached.
customer: VPs of supply chain and transportation procurement at mid-market shippers with $5M-$80M in truckload spend across 8-100 facilities (food and beverage, building products, paper and packaging, PE-backed manufacturers). Secondary: PE operating partners. A second product goes to brokers as a pre-quote facility difficulty score.
problem: Shippers think their rates reflect lane and market. Brokers know the rate also carries a facility premium for long dwell, no appointments, lumper games, no restrooms or parking, and dock staff who vanish at lunch. Our quotes to those docks quietly run $50-$300 a load higher, or the load is skipped by carriers and covered at the last minute at a spot premium. The shipper never sees it because it is buried in the broker's margin, and the broker profits from it, so the broker will never tell them.
solution: Pool anonymized quote-request, time-to-cover, rate-versus-benchmark and carrier-decline-reason data from 10-30 participating small brokers, who get a free facility difficulty score for pre-quoting in return. Run a regression of rate against market benchmark with facility fixed effects. Add dwell data from ELD partners or driver surveys. Deliver a Dock Tax Report: per-facility annualized premium in dollars, ranked, with a fix playbook (appointment windows, extended hours, drop-trailer conversion, driver amenities, lumper policy) and a re-bid plan on the affected lanes.
why_now: Driver supply has tightened through 2025-26 enforcement (English-proficiency out-of-service enforcement, non-domiciled CDL restrictions, authority revocations), which makes carriers pickier about which docks they will visit. AI arrival prediction and automated detention data from TMS integrations are making dwell data cheap. Vendor sources report that moving from first-come-first-served to scheduled appointments cuts dwell 30-50% within about 90 days, so the fix is proven and the ROI is easy to state.
revenue_model: $15K-$40K per shipper report or quarterly engagement, or 15-20% of first-year verified savings. Broker-side subscription of $200-$500/month for pre-quote facility scores builds the data flywheel.
non_obvious_insight: The dock tax is the only freight cost that is invisible to the payer and visible to everyone else. Every broker keeps a mental list of facilities where they never quote under a floor, and colleagues have nicknames for them, but nobody has priced that list for the shipper. Shippers will trust a neutral third party far more than their own broker, because the broker earns from the premium.
first_30_days: Get 8 brokers to share 90 days of anonymized quote and cover data for 20 named facilities in a shared sheet. Build the first regression by hand in a notebook. Cold-message 30 transportation directors on LinkedIn with a free 'your three worst docks' teaser built from the pooled data and public driver reviews, and sell 3 pilots at $7.5K. Give contributing brokers a per-facility difficulty lookup so they keep feeding the pool.

title: Cash-Flow Lifeline for K-12 Service Vendors
one_liner: Same-week invoice funding for small vendors who serve schools (after-school, tutoring, therapy, van companies), priced using each district's known payment calendar, with a service-continuity guarantee for principals.
customer: Small K-12 vendors paying a financing fee: after-school providers, contract speech, occupational and counseling practices, tutoring companies, small van and transportation contractors, and arts and PE providers. Principals are the sponsor and the free channel.
problem: Districts pay invoices 60 to 120 days late, and federal-grant reimbursements (21st Century, Title programs) lag further. Small vendors run out of cash and vanish in October, mid-year, leaving kids without services. Principals cannot legally pay faster and get blamed when the therapist stops coming. Generic factoring companies price district risk like a private customer or refuse it.
solution: Fund invoices within 48 hours at 90 percent advance. Verification is a text or QR 'services delivered' confirmation from the principal, which is the step district accounts payable needs anyway. Price risk using each district's board-approval calendar, warrant runs and reimbursement cycles, which we assemble from public board minutes. Add a continuity guarantee: if a funded vendor fails, a pre-vetted bench vendor steps in. Districts get a simple notice-of-assignment form to sign.
why_now: The July 2025 withholding of roughly $6.8B in federal education funds, released weeks later, showed how fragile the timing is. Post-ESSER budgets are tight, and small-business credit is harder for vendors with slow government customers. LLMs can now read board packets, purchase orders and approval calendars at scale to predict pay dates.
revenue_model: Fee of about 1.5 to 3 percent per invoice per 30 days advanced, plus a vendor subscription ($99 per month) for the delivery-confirmation and invoicing workflow.
non_obvious_insight: District default risk is near zero. The risk is timing, and timing is predictable if you know how boards and warrant runs work. The principal's confirmation, not the bank, is the bottleneck, so whoever owns that step owns the data. Investors dismiss K-12 as slow and poor, but the payer is a taxing authority, which is the safest receivable there is.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 small vendors from principals' and coordinators' contact lists, starting with after-school and therapy contractors that have already had payment problems. Raise $150k to $300k of angel or warehouse capital and fund the first invoices at a flat fee. Build the district payment calendars in a spreadsheet from public minutes, which becomes the pricing model and the data moat.

title: Fresh-Address Desk for Medicaid Plans
one_liner: Turn Title I front offices into a consent-based channel that keeps families on Medicaid, paid per household retained by health plans and hospitals, with a revenue share to the school.
customer: Medicaid managed care plans (member retention and quality-bonus teams) and nonprofit hospitals with community-benefit budgets. Principals and PTAs are the channel partners and receive a revenue share. They do not pay.
problem: Six-month renewals and work-requirement paperwork are scheduled to hit expansion-adult Medicaid enrollees in 2027. Plans lose members when renewal mail goes to old addresses and phone numbers, and their call-center contact rates are dismal. Kids often lose coverage in the household churn even when they stay eligible. Plans cannot reach the families who most need help, and the parent hears the plan's mail as junk.
solution: A text-first, home-language 'update your info and check your renewal' flow built into the school's existing August packet and registration. A part-time parent-liaison 'benefits desk' sits in the front office a few hours a week. Data goes to a plan only with a signed opt-in parent consent, not under FERPA directory information. Plans pay a fee per verified address or phone update and per completed renewal. About 30 percent of the revenue goes to a school-controlled discretionary fund. The same desk later handles other bounty-paying programs: utility low-income enrollment, Lifeline phone and internet plans, Summer EBT, and vision and dental follow-up.
why_now: Under the 2025 budget reconciliation law, expansion-adult redeterminations move to every 6 months after the end of 2026 and work requirements begin in 2027, unless states get a delay. The post-COVID Medicaid unwinding showed that most coverage losses were procedural. Principals are also hungry for discretionary dollars after the 2025 federal freezes and cancelled school-mental-health grants.
revenue_model: Per-household bounty of roughly $25 to $75 for a verified update or completed renewal. Plans also pay an annual per-school or per-region program fee. Optional add-on bounties from utilities and phone carriers.
non_obvious_insight: The freshest address and phone database of low-income families is not held by any agency. It is held by the school secretary, who re-verifies it every August because busing, lunch and emergency cards depend on it. Families ignore the plan's letters but answer the office they trust. Principals will only say yes if the money flows back to the school and consent is explicit, and that design is the moat.
first_30_days: Pick one state and call the community-engagement or quality director at two or three Medicaid plans. Offer a 90-day pilot in 3 schools whose principals you already know, priced per verified update. Build it with Twilio and a bilingual part-timer, and use a hashed list-match to show how many of a plan's returned-mail members appear in school records. Have the principal co-sign a one-page consent form that PTA volunteers can hand out.

title: Rebuild-Cost Audit Sold Through Agents' E&O Fear
one_liner: A 15-minute independent rebuild-cost check at renewal that documents limits, sold to the agents and E&O carriers who hold the underinsurance tail.
customer: Independent agencies in California, Colorado and Florida and their E&O program managers. Wealth advisors and trust attorneys for high-value homes are a second channel.
problem: In the Palisades, insurer estimates run about $462/sq ft against contractor budgets up to $1,065, and only about 13% of owners have started rebuilding. Part of that gap is contractor premium, but a large part is stale valuation. Owners are underinsured, and the agents who sold the limits carry E&O exposure. Renewals in 2026-27 are the moment to fix it.
solution: A rebuild reality check that pulls permit records, local bid data, post-disaster cost surge and home features. It outputs a defensible range and recommended limits or extended replacement cost, with contractor validation for the top decile of homes. It is white-labeled by the agent, and the audit log doubles as an E&O defense file.
why_now: The LA fire claims experience is now public and quantified, so E&O carriers and agencies finally have a concrete loss to point at.
revenue_model: $29-99 per policy to the agency, or a program fee from an E&O carrier that gives premium credits. A $299 tier adds a contractor walk-through.
non_obvious_insight: The economic buyer is not the homeowner but the agent's E&O carrier, who wants documentation. Underinsurance is the biggest unpriced tail left after the LA fires.
first_30_days: Calibrate on 100 posted Palisades and Altadena claim outcomes. Pitch 5 agencies with high-value books, and approach one agency E&O program manager about a documented-audit premium credit.

title: Prospecting for Brackish Aquifers Like Gold
one_liner: A water-exploration company that maps, options and permits high-yield brackish and fresh aquifers before developers need them, then sells or leases 'water-ready' sites and supply.
customer: Data-center developers, small towns and rural districts, ranchers and industrial parks needing 1-5 MGD of defensible supply. Buyers pay for studies, and later for site options and supply contracts.
problem: About 1,800 ERCOT projects are held, and water is the new gating item. Siting decisions are still made on power and fiber first, and water studies come late from generalist consultants. Groundwater in Texas is private property under the rule of capture subject to local district rules (my understanding), so early options on proven supply are valuable, yet almost nobody is exploring for water the way miners explore for minerals.
solution: Use public airborne-electromagnetic surveys, well logs and machine learning to map the probability of high-yield brackish aquifers. Option land and water rights, drill test wells, obtain production permits, and pair with a treatment partner. Sell paid site reports first, then options and long-term supply.
why_now: Drone-borne electromagnetic surveys are getting cheap, brackish desalination costs are falling, and regulators are blocking new load without a proven water plan.
revenue_model: $15-75k paid site studies, drilling programs on cost-plus or success fee, and $1-5M site-option or supply sales.
non_obvious_insight: Water rights are the new mineral rights. The geophysics is becoming a commodity, but the permitting playbook and early option positions are not.
first_30_days: Sell five 'water-ready screening' reports at $15-25k to developers in the ERCOT queue and to towns, using public data only. Line up a drilling partner and identify two parcels near transmission with promising brackish aquifers to option.

title: Pre-Loss Home Reconstruction Dossiers for Insurance Claims
one_liner: Rebuild, in the exact quality and condition language insurers can't wave away, what a destroyed home actually had, using old appraisals, listing photos, permits and imagery.
customer: Public adjusters and policyholder-side insurance attorneys handling total-loss wildfire, hurricane and tornado claims pay $900-2,500 per dossier. Direct-to-homeowner is $495 for a basic version. Independent insurance agents later buy a 'pre-loss baseline' for their high-value clients.
problem: After a total loss, the insurer's estimate assumes builder-grade finishes and smaller square footage. The survivor's photos and receipts burned, so 'like kind and quality' becomes a memory-versus-spreadsheet fight worth tens or hundreds of thousands of dollars per house. Public adjusters reconstruct from Zillow photos and homeowner recollection, which adjusters on the other side discount.
solution: A retrospective, signed 'as-was' dossier delivered in about 5 business days. Sources: (1) any prior purchase or refinance appraisal the homeowner has (borrowers are entitled to copies) or can get through the lender or servicer; (2) archived MLS photos and remarks from the last sale; (3) permit and remodel history; (4) assessor quality and size records; (5) historical aerial and street-level imagery. A licensed appraiser assigns the standard Q1-Q6 quality and C1-C6 condition ratings, lists the finishes and features, and estimates replacement cost at that quality level.
why_now: The January 2025 Los Angeles fires destroyed roughly 16,000 structures, and many claims are still being contested in late 2026. Every wildfire and hurricane season adds more total losses. Insurers are tightening costs and leaning on adjuster software. Photo and record archives from prior sales are now digital and searchable, so the reconstruction is a 5-day job.
revenue_model: Flat fee per dossier only. USPAP forbids contingent appraisal fees, and independence is the product's credibility. Volume pricing for public adjuster firms. $99/yr 'baseline vault' (current LiDAR, photos and Q/C ratings) sold through independent insurance agents in wildfire and hurricane zones, who carry E&O exposure when clients are underinsured.
non_obvious_insight: The best pre-loss evidence in America already exists, sitting in lender closing files, appraisal workfiles kept five years and old MLS pages. Nobody connects it to claims. A neutral licensed appraiser's dated interior photos and Q/C ratings carry far more weight with an insurer than a homeowner's testimony. Those disputes are won at the finish level (cabinetry, flooring, millwork), not on square footage, and the appraiser's rating vocabulary is what claims examiners recognize.
first_30_days: Recruit 3 appraisers in Los Angeles County who lost work. Build one dossier template. Offer 5 free pilot dossiers to 2-3 public adjuster firms and one policyholder attorney working Altadena or Pacific Palisades cases, and measure how much the insurer's revised offer moves. Then charge $1,500 per dossier and use the measured lift as the sales pitch.

title: Restock Monitors Turned Competitor Sell-Through Radar
one_liner: Repurpose the Discord restock-monitor infrastructure teen resellers run into a SKU- and size-level sell-through index for DTC brands and the investors and acquirers who buy them.
customer: Founders and merchandisers of DTC brands who want to see rivals' sell-through ($199 to $799 per month), boutique retail buyers, and consumer-focused funds, search-fund buyers and e-commerce acquirers who need diligence on a Shopify brand ($2,000 to $5,000 per report).
problem: Everyone in e-commerce has to guess how fast a competitor's hero product actually sells. Public analytics tools give traffic estimates, not sell-through by size, color or restock. Buyers of small Shopify brands take the seller's word for 'we sell out in days' and get burned.
solution: Teen resellers already run monitors on thousands of storefronts: each one polls public product feeds so a Discord ping fires the instant a size restocks. The same stream, kept as history, shows how fast each variant flips to sold-out, restock cadence, drop timing, markdown timing, price changes and collection moves. Package it as a weekly Sold-Out Index and an on-demand brand report: 'their black M hoodie sold out in 41 minutes twice, restocked every 3 weeks, and they cut price 15% after the tariff news'. Use public storefront signals only, with no checkout tricks, and honor rate limits and terms.
why_now: Tariff-driven price changes in 2025-26 have every brand asking what rivals did to prices and when. DTC brand acquisition and roll-up activity means more diligence is being done on tiny Shopify brands. LLMs now classify messy product titles into a clean taxonomy cheaply, which was the hard part of turning monitor pings into an index.
revenue_model: Subscription for brand and retail buyers ($199 to $799 per month), one-off diligence reports ($2,000 to $5,000), and a data feed for funds later.
non_obvious_insight: The restock-alert economy is really an accidental, huge, always-on sensor network for the long tail of DTC commerce. Enterprise alt-data vendors ignore small brands because they think there is no data on them. Resellers have been logging exactly that data every minute for years. The unit of value is sold-out speed by variant, which reseller monitors track and analytics vendors do not.
first_30_days: Take the existing monitor feed for about 2,000 storefronts in streetwear, sneakers and collectibles and start logging history now, because history is the asset. Publish a free weekly Sold-Out Index thread on TikTok and X to get inbound. Sell 10 founders a $199 competitor watchlist by DM. Pitch one search-fund or acquirer community for a paid diligence report at $2,000 to check willingness to pay.

title: Human Callback Line Sold Through Credit Unions
one_liner: A staffed 'is this really my grandson?' phone line and call-screening kit for members over 70, paid for per enrolled member by community credit unions whose deposits walk out the door in voice-clone scams.
customer: Community banks and credit unions with $300M-$5B in assets and an older membership, paying about $3-6 per enrolled member per month. A secondary direct-to-family tier is $12 per month paid by adult children.
problem: Voice cloning needs only a few seconds of audio, and older adults are losing large sums to family-emergency and impersonation scams. The FBI reportedly counted about $352M in AI-linked fraud losses among people over 60 in 2025, and the FTC estimates most fraud goes unreported. Victims are shamed and rushed, and the scam's whole design is to prevent a pause. Most transfers are authorized, so banks are usually not liable, but the member's savings leave the institution and often end up in a crypto ATM.
solution: A screen-free service: one memorable number on a fridge magnet and phone sticker. Whenever anyone calls asking for money or urgency, the member hangs up and calls the line. A trained human (retired tellers, 911 dispatchers, nurses) runs a slow 5-minute out-of-band check: pre-registered family safe word, a call-back to the real relative through their stored circle, and a plain-language 'this matches a known scam script' verdict. Members with large cash withdrawals or wires get a teller prompt that says 'want to call the line first?', with the credit union's flag visible to the desk. Enrollment happens at branches and senior centers with a 20-minute family safe-word ritual.
why_now: Voice-clone scams have moved from novelty to mainstream in 2025-26. Regulators, state elder-exploitation reporting duties and the UK's mandatory reimbursement rules for authorized push-payment fraud point the direction US institutions are heading. Credit unions are competing on trust and member service against fintech, and have no good product for the fraud they cannot block.
revenue_model: B2B2C per-enrolled-member fee ($3-6 per month) with a pilot flat fee of about $2,000 per month per credit union; overage for call volume; $12 per month direct-to-family plan; optional add-on to sell to insurers of members' homes and autos.
non_obvious_insight: Against a perfect fake voice, the only durable defense is a slow, human, out-of-band ritual, and the buyer is not the senior but the institution holding the money. The scam is a deposit-flight event, and credit unions have the branch relationship, field-of-membership community ties and senior-center access to reach victims before the scammer does. Making the 'moment of doubt' land on a number people already trust is cheaper than any AI detector.
first_30_days: Pitch one sub-$1B credit union through its CEO or member-experience lead (reach them via state credit union league events and CUNA meetups). Recruit 8 retired tellers and dispatchers to staff phone shifts from home using Twilio and a shared inbox, with no engineering needed. Enroll 60 seniors from a local senior center in a 60-day pilot and log every attempted scam reported. Sell the results as a member-perk pilot at $2,000 per month.
